claims.statement: pytest is the project's only automated correctness gate: no linter or type-checker is configured, AGENTS.md states correctness is enforced by the test suite, pyproject.toml points pytest at the tests directory, and the standard invocations are `python -m pytest -q` and `HAAP_REPO=/path/to/haap python -m pytest -q` for the compat test.

tests/conftest.py makes the package importable from a plain checkout by inserting <repo>/src at sys.path position 0 on import, so tests run without `pip install -e .`; each phase test file repeats the same sys.path insertion at its top so files also run standalone.

The make_server factory fixture boots a real DirectoryHTTPServer per call on 127.0.0.1 at an OS-assigned ephemeral port using the same production construction path (DirectoryHTTPServer.build with a DirectoryConfig, fresh directory KeyPair, the shared MutableClock, and an optional resolver), a per-test SQLite DB under tmp_path, and generous default rate limits (rate_register_per_hour=100_000, rate_search_per_min=100_000) so multi-agent tests are not throttled while dedicated abuse tests override them; created servers are stopped in fixture teardown.

`running` (make_server()) and `running_full` (make_server(max_agents=1), which targets the DIRECTORY_FULL 503 path) are the ready-made single-server fixtures; both return a RunningServer dataclass exposing url, server, clock, config and resolver, so tests assert over real HTTP while observing internals such as server.service.store, server.service.keypair, server.service.audit, running.config and running.clock.

All servers built inside one test share the single function-scoped clock fixture, a MutableClock callable starting at 1_700_000_000.0 whose advance(seconds) moves time forward; because store and service read now exclusively through the injected Clock (production default timeutil.system_clock), TTL expiry, challenge/token expiry, report tenure and checkpoint cadence are exercised deterministically without sleeping, and a server restarted on the same DB with the same advanced clock prunes expired entries during DirectoryService construction.

StubResolver implements the injectable Resolver.check(domain, method, token) seam (a Protocol in resolver.py, backed in production by SystemResolver delegating to verify.check_dns_txt via system dig and verify.check_https_well_known via stdlib TLS) using in-memory maps — txt keyed by `_haap.<domain>` accepting the bare token or a `haap-verify=<token>` record, well_known keyed by domain accepting the exact body or JSON `haap_verify_token`, and a txt_temporary set forcing the transient DNS failure — raising the same stable DirectoryError codes as the real checks (DNS_ERROR_TEMPORARY, DNS_TXT_NOT_FOUND, WELL_KNOWN_NOT_FOUND, WELL_KNOWN_MISMATCH).

The Agent fixture (with the make_agent factory, which always mints a fresh KeyPair) models a directory participant: fingerprint and public_key_b64 derive from the Ed25519 keypair; manifest(**overrides) builds a valid haap-public-manifest-v1 document; sign_manifest signs the frozen canonical JSON (json.dumps sort_keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=False) exactly as the server verifies; sign_nonce signs challenge-proof and heartbeat strings; and sign_payload signs the canonical JSON of the request subset the server verifies for the L2/L3/L4 endpoints.

http_post and http_get are urllib helpers returning (status, parsed JSON body) for both success and HTTPError, so rejection tests assert the exact (HTTP status, error.code) pair in one step, and register_agent drives the full three-step /v1 registration flow (submit signed manifest, sign the returned nonce, complete with endpoint proof) returning the completion body.

Test file names map to the F0–F6 build plan in the README status table: test_store.py covers F0 (health boot, audit genesis, persistence across restart, CLI-over-file-over-env config precedence, live count), test_registration.py covers F1 (proof-of-endpoint registration happy path, the rejection set with stable codes, update-vs-fresh and re-register-after-expiry semantics), and test_search_heartbeat.py covers F2 (AND free-text, geo radius, pagination and limit clamp, v1 signed plus legacy unsigned heartbeat, injected-clock expiry pruned on read and on startup).

F3 domain verification is split across test_domain.py, which runs the whole L2 protocol over StubResolver (202 token issuance, DNS TXT and HTTPS well-known happy paths, DNS_TXT_NOT_FOUND 422, DOMAIN_ENDPOINT_MISMATCH 422, VERIFICATION_EXPIRED 410, VERIFICATION_USED 409, SIGNATURE_MISMATCH 400, VERIFICATION_LIMIT_REACHED 429, and the 90-day downgrade), and test_domain_verification.py, which unit-tests the real verify.py parsers with no network (validate_domain rules, registrable_domain, dig answer-line parsing over static text) plus HTTP edge cases (DOMAIN_INVALID 400, unknown method as INVALID_SCHEMA 400, AGENT_NOT_LISTED 404, and confirm being retryable — a failed confirm does not consume the verification_id).

F4 is split across test_vouching.py (L3: create/read/revoke, VOUCHEE_NOT_LISTED 404, VOUCH_EXPIRED and VOUCH_INVALID 400, duplicate VOUCH_EXISTS 409, the vouch_max_outgoing cap as VOUCH_LIMIT_REACHED 429, and /v1/trust/paths depth-2 traversal) and test_reputation.py (L4: young reporters recorded with counts_toward_automation false, REPORT_EXISTS 409, TARGET_NOT_LISTED 404, three eligible abuse-class reports auto-suspending a target so it disappears from anonymous profile and search while /health reports suspended, non-abuse classes never auto-suspending, moderator takedown with MODERATOR_UNKNOWN and TAKEDOWN_UNAUTHORIZED 403, and the suspend/appeal/unsuspend cycle).

F5 audit transparency is covered by test_audit_chain.py (each mutation appends at least one audit entry, the chain starts at genesis and audit.verify_chain recomputes every hash and linkage, /v1/audit/log is contiguous, tampering with a stored field breaks verification, and entries carry only a 64-hex detail_hash never a detail body) and test_checkpoints.py (audit head and responses signed by the directory key with X-HAAP-Directory-Signature and X-HAAP-Directory-Fingerprint, create/list/verify of checkpoints, maybe_checkpoint cadence advanced through the clock, /v1/audit/verify, the redacted per-agent audit view, and a final checkpoint written on shutdown).

F6 operations are covered by test_ops_federation.py: /metrics renders Prometheus text with haapd_agents_listed, haapd_audit_seq, haapd_ops_total and per-code rejection counters such as haapd_rejections_total{code="RATE_LIMITED"}; a dedicated low-limit server proves the register flood returns 429 with a Retry-After header; and mirror.ingest_chain downloads /v1/audit/log, verifies linkage locally and reproduces the served head.

test_proxy_headers.py pins the per-IP rate-limit keying rules: with trust_proxy_headers false (default) spoofed X-Forwarded-For values share the single loopback bucket and are throttled together, and with trust_proxy_headers true http_api._client_ip honors CF-Connecting-IP or X-Forwarded-For only when the TCP peer is 127.0.0.1 or ::1, giving each distinct external client its own bucket while a headerless request falls back to the loopback peer.

test_compat_client.py proves the unmodified companion haap client works against this service (haap.identity.IdentityStore plus haap.registry_client register, legacy unsigned heartbeat, and capability/free-text search) and is skipped — not failed — when the client package is absent: _find_haap_repo resolves HAAP_REPO or the sibling ../haap checkout by checking for haap/registry_client.py, pytestmark skipif carries the explanation, and the found checkout is inserted into sys.path.

Tests never touch real DNS or the network: the L2 dns_txt path, which shells out to the system dig binary in production, is exercised only through the injectable resolver seam via StubResolver, and the real dig/well-known parser code is unit-tested against static dig-output text and in-memory well-known bodies.

Every rejection test asserts the exact stable code and HTTP status pair, which works because the suite's HTTP helpers return status plus the parsed error envelope and because errors.py:ERROR_STATUS is the add-only master table mapping each DirectoryError code to its fixed HTTP status.
